notes: Line-by-line read of every new sentence. The nhs.uk search surfaced NHS trust warfarin leaflets rather than the national anticoagulants pages; excerpts support: bleeding and bruising as the main effect, hair loss/rash less often, vitamin K-rich foods lower the INR so consistency not avoidance, grapefruit and other juices raise the INR, alcohol kept within weekly limits and binge drinking avoided, antibiotics/illness/vomiting/diarrhoea/OTC products change the INR and are reported to the clinic. No INR target, dose, or titration figure was added (targets 2-3 / 2.5-3.5, 3-5 day onset and 4-12 week monitoring predate the patch). Boxed warning, narrow therapeutic index, calciphylaxis, inherited resistance, breastfeeding compatibility, rodenticide history and DOAC intracranial-bleed comparison (consistent with the pre-patch apixaban record) are StatPearls/MedlinePlus general knowledge stated descriptively. Interruption before surgery and warfarin-DOAC switching are framed as clinic-managed, not as instructions. No protected field changed.
